title: Confounding in the association of proton pump inhibitor use with risk of community-acquired pneumonia
authors: Jena AB, Sun E, Goldman DP
population: Members of six private US health plans: 26,436 who filled at least one PPI prescription and 28,054 who never did
funder: National Institute on Aging. The design, conduct, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of the data are the responsibility of the investigators, with no involvement from the funding sources.
authorConflicts: The authors declare that they do not have a conflict of interest.
result: Falsification analysis. Among PPI users, quarters with a filled PPI prescription had higher adjusted rates than quarters without of community-acquired pneumonia (111 against 68 per 10,000), chest pain (597 against 336) and urinary tract infection (186 against 151), all p<0.001; PPI users also had higher rates than non-users in quarters without a prescription (pneumonia 68 against 61 per 10,000). Associations with conditions without a known pathophysiological link indicate that the association with pneumonia may be confounded.
